chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd ibn Abd Allah both narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of his father, and al-Husayn ibn Sa'd, and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, on the authority of Ibn Abu Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, that I entered into the presence of Abu Abdillah (AS)

so he asked me: 'Can you describe Allah?' I replied, 'Yes.' He said: 'Give it.' I said: 'He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' He said: 'This is an attribute shared by the created.' I asked: 'Then how do you describe Him?' He said: 'He is Light with no darkness in Him, Ever-Living with no death in Him, Knowing with no ignorance in Him, Truth with no falsehood in Him.' I left from his presence and I was the most learned of people regarding Divine Unity.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq describe the attributes of Allah in contrast to created beings?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the Shia theological distinction between attributes shared with creation (like hearing and seeing) and those unique to the Divine Essence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the concept of *Tawhid* by emphasizing absolute perfection through the negation of opposites—Light without darkness, Life without death—thereby affirming God’s transcendence (*Tanzih*) while maintaining His knowability. This approach aligns with the school of the Ahl al-Bayt’s nuanced balance between affirming divine attributes and rejecting anthropomorphism.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 14. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah both said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of his father and al-Husayn ibn Sa`d and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim that I entered into the presence of Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

so he asked me: “Can you describe Allah?” Hence, I replied, “Yes.” He (AS) said: “Give me your description.” So, I answered, “He is the All-Hearing and the All-Seeing.” He (AS) explained, “There are attributes which equally apply to the created.” I asked, “Then how do you describe Him?” Thus, he (AS) said: “He is Light as there is no darkness in Him. He is Ever-Living as there is no death in Him. He is the Omniscient as there is no ignorance in Him, and He is the Truth as there is no false in Him.” Then I left from his presence and I was the most learned of people with regard to Divine Unity.
